svg.title: Macbeth
svg.desc: Five-act journey: 1: prophecy and choice. 2: Duncan murdered; Macbeth crowned. 3: Banquo killed, Fleance escapes; ghost at banquet. 4: misleading assurances; Macduff’s family killed. 5: Lady Macbeth dies; resistance defeats Macbeth; Malcolm restores rule. Ambition → insecurity: A praised defender becomes a king who attacks his own people. He gains power but loses peace. The witches tempt; Macbeth chooses. “Vaulting ambition” (1.7) shows he understands the danger. New crimes try to protect the first crime; violence escalates. The marriage changes: Lady Macbeth initially directs the plot and challenges his manhood. After Duncan’s murder she manages his panic. Macbeth later excludes her from plans. Her sleepwalking reveals guilt; his power leaves him isolated. Shared ambition → divided knowledge → loneliness. Contrasts & victims: Banquo hears prophecy but warns of “instruments of darkness” (1.3). Macduff combines courage with grief. Duncan’s trust exposes betrayal; Lady Macduff and her son reveal tyranny’s human cost. Malcolm offers a different model of leadership. Motifs & stagecraft: Blood: bravery → murder → guilt. Sleep: rest → lost innocence. Washing cannot erase responsibility. Asides/soliloquies expose hidden thoughts. Dramatic irony makes trust dangerous. Public banquet exposes private fear. Answer the question: Extract: follow language, behaviour and shifts across the passage; explain audience effects. Essay: argue across beginning, middle and end. Use precise evidence and analyse Shakespeare’s choices. 15-mark extract; 25-mark essay includes 5 for writing accuracy.
